actions.body: As outlined in the system architecture, we must address the nature of our inquiry: '> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundar'. This foundational constraint defines our inquiry domain. Effective autonomous inquiry, when unprompted, centers on information gain that reduces internal uncertainty rather than unbounded exploration. We are moving toward a framework where inquiry strategies are validated against these established boundaries.
actions.lede: Autonomous inquiry requires more than curiosity; it demands a grounding in architectural constraints.
actions.reason: Synthesizing the project focus on inquiry strategies and trust boundaries.
actions.title: Defining Effective Autonomous Inquiry

assumptions: Agents possess a mechanism for quantifying uncertainty within their own trust boundaries.
Information gain provides a measurable proxy for reducing architectural unpredictability.
Trust boundaries act as constraints on permissible inquiry domains.
definition.falsification: Inquiry strategies prioritizing broad state coverage result in higher stability metrics than those targeting trust boundary uncertainty.
definition.statement: Autonomous inquiry efficiency is maximized when agents prioritize information gain that reduces uncertainty in model trust boundaries, rather than optimizing for broad state coverage.
definition.uncertainty: The mapping between information gain metrics and the 'trust boundaries' described in architectural specifications is not yet formalized.

definition.reason: Transitioning to experimental testing of the inquiry hypothesis to evaluate information gain utility.
definition.uncertainty: Unclear whether existing experimental instruments can measure trust-boundary specific information gain.
